commands.review_summary:
The PR adds a 30-second command-queue starvation threshold, scans queued entries by effective priority at dequeue, exports the threshold, and adds fake-timer tests for aged background ordering.

PR surface: Source +53, Tests +71. Total +124 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection reproduces the current-main gap because static priority insertion drains with `state.queue.shift()`, and the PR-specific defect is source-reproducible because `priority + 1` makes aged normal work foreground-equivalent.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Manual review is needed because the repair depends on scheduler-policy approval and the contributor still needs to provide current-head real behavior proof.

target.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue
target.body:
Fixes #79589

## Problem

Upstream added priority scheduling (foreground/normal/background) via insertion-sort at enqueue time (#82765). Within a static priority tier, older background work can still sit behind later background work indefinitely when the lane stays busy.

## Fix

Implement a **foreground-preserving one-tier aging** policy:

- After `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS` (30s), an entry is promoted by **exactly one priority tier** (`priority + 1`).
- Background (-1) ages to normal (0), still below fresh foreground (1).
- Fresh user/foreground work always runs before aged background.
- Aged background still beats fresh background at the same static priority.

This intentionally does **not** promote aged work to `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` or above fresh foreground. The contract is fairness among same-or-lower tiers without starving interactive work.

Files:
- `lanes.ts`: export `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS`
- `command-queue.ts`: `effectivePriority()` (+1 after threshold) and `pickNextIndex()` (effective priority, then oldest enqueue time, then sequence)
- `command-queue.test.ts`: one-tier aging regression tests using `enqueueCommandInLane(CommandLane.Main, ...)`

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Command-lane drain selects aged background before fresh background after 30s, while still preferring fresh foreground over aged background (one-tier aging).

**Real environment tested:** macOS, Node from the local OpenClaw checkout, branch `feat/command-queue-priority` at head `41cd18a776`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
cd /tmp/oc-75299
node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/process/command-queue.test.ts -t "aged background"
```

**Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched branch:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/process/command-queue.test.ts -t "aged background"
 ✓ command queue > preserves foreground priority over aged background work
 ✓ command queue > promotes aged background above fresh background (one-tier starvation guard)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 30 skipped (32)
```

Source confirmation of the one-tier policy:

```console
$ grep -n "STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS\|return entry.priority" src/process/lanes.ts src/process/command-queue.ts
src/process/lanes.ts:15:export const STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS = 30_000;
src/process/command-queue.ts:282:  if (Date.now() - entry.enqueuedAt >= STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS) {
src/process/command-queue.ts:283:    return entry.priority + 1;
src/process/command-queue.ts:285:  return entry.priority;
```

Behavioral contract exercised by the two tests:
1. Aged background then fresh foreground drain order: `["foreground", "background"]`
2. Aged background then fresh background drain order: `["aged-bg", "fresh-bg"]`

**Observed result after fix:** One-tier aging raises background to normal after 30s so it beats later background work, while fresh foreground still wins over aged background. Policy, comments, tests, and this proof describe the same contract.

**What was not tested:** Live gateway under wall-clock multi-session contention with real cron/foreground traffic.
